parsed.use_case: Tracking the longest uninterrupted sequence of distinct transactions or unique device identifiers in high-throughput telemetry logs to quantify peak bursts of collision-free activity.
system_examples: Network security monitoring systems — inspecting contiguous packet sequences to determine the longest unbroken span of unique connection nonces to flag replay attacks and session collisions.
Real-time event streaming pipelines — identifying the longest continuous sequence of records with distinct event identifiers to measure burst capacity and audit stream integrity.
parsed.explanation: The optimal solution uses a sliding window with two pointers alongside a hash map that records the most recent index of each character, advancing the left boundary immediately past any duplicate. This reduces the runtime from a naive O(n³) or O(n²) substring-checking approach to a single O(n) linear pass with O(min(n, alphabet_size)) auxiliary space. In production, this pattern is fundamental for streaming systems that must track dynamic state and detect boundary conditions in real time without buffering or rescanning historic data.
